Config basics
A config groups its tweaks, servers, access rules, and user-facing information. Name is required. Access restrictions apply to imported or non-owner users; they do not restrict the config owner. Open Advanced Options for access controls and Extra for resource-sharing options.

What imported users may edit
• Unlock Server: Allows imported users to edit server connection values.
• Unlock Server Credentials: Keeps the server endpoint protected but allows imported users to enter or replace server credentials. It works together with Unlock Server.
• Unlock Payload: Allows payload, SNI, TLS version, DNSTT resolver/payload, and V2Ray Bug Host changes.
• Unlock Proxy: Allows the tweak proxy to be changed.
• Unlock All: Transfers config ownership to the importing device after all import checks pass. It disables the other restrictions, so enable it only when full ownership transfer is intended.

Access and device checks
• Password: Requires users to provide the config password.
• Device ID Lock: Allows only listed Device IDs. Separate multiple IDs with semicolons, for example ID1;ID2.
• Expiry Date: Prevents non-owner use after the selected date.
• Mobile Locked: Requires a mobile-data connection.
• Block Root / Jailbreak: Prevents use on rooted Android devices or jailbroken iPhones.
• Store Install: Requires an official store install (Google Play on Android, App Store on iPhone).
• Block Application: Blocks use when any listed Android app is installed. Enter an app display name or package name, and separate multiple entries with semicolons or new lines, for example WhatsApp;com.example.app.

Updates and Web Panel
• Update URL: Enter a complete valid URL used to deliver config updates.
• Panel Username: Assigns the Web Panel user who may remotely manage this config.
• Enable the Cloud option beside Password, Device ID, or Update URL to manage that value through the Web Panel instead of storing a local value in this form. Selecting Cloud also requires Panel Username.

Resources and customization
• Share Resources: Makes the tweaks and servers in this config available to other configs.
• Show Shared: Displays tweaks and servers shared by other configs here.
• Custom Resources: Allows non-owner users to add their own local tweaks and servers for this config only.
• Hide SSH Banner: Hides the SSH server banner when supported by the connection.

A server stores the endpoint and credentials used by a compatible tweak. Enter a required name (up to 100 characters), choose the tunnel family and subtype, and complete the visible fields.

IPv4, IPv6, and multiple values
• Combined endpoint fields use host1;host2:port@username:password. Separate candidates with semicolons; one is selected when connecting.
• IPv4 and host names need no brackets. Bracket IPv6 when a port follows it: [2001:db8::10]:22@username:password.
• Multiple IPv6 candidates are valid: [2001:db8::10];[2001:db8::11]:22@username:password.
• In V2Ray manual mode, enter a raw IPv6 address without brackets because Port has its own field.
• Do not add http:// or https:// to host-only fields. Authentication is separated at the first colon, so a password may contain additional colons.

OpenVPN / SSH
• Normal and SSL ports: One server can be reused by Direct, HTTP/payload, proxy, and SSL/TLS tweaks. Put the normal service port with the server host; put the TLS port in SSL Port.
• OpenVPN: Select TCP or UDP and enter credentials as username:password. Paste a valid OpenVPN client config or use Import .ovpn; imported config text is validated and limited to 1 MB. A remote line may use semicolon-separated hosts and must keep the normal OpenVPN port. Private Key is optional.
• SSH: Use host1;host2:port@username:password and put the normal SSH port there; it defaults to 22 when omitted. An optional private key must be a PEM key containing a BEGIN ... KEY header.
• SSL Port defaults to 443 and is used only by SSL/TLS flows.

Examples
• SSH: ssh.example.com:22@username:password with SSL Port 443. Keep 22 with the host so non-SSL tweaks continue to work.
• OpenVPN TCP: keep remote vpn.example.com 1194 in the config and enter 443 in SSL Port. Direct, HTTP/payload, and non-SSL proxy tweaks use 1194; SSL/TLS flows use 443.

V2Ray
• Config mode: Paste JSON or a supported share link: vmess://, vless://, trojan://, ss://, hysteria2://, or hy2://. Use the paste, clear, and mode controls beside the config field.
• Manual mode: Supported types are Default, VLESS, VMess, Shadowsocks, Socks, HTTP, Trojan, Hysteria2, and WireGuard.
• Address/Host and Port identify the endpoint. Fill the credentials shown for the selected protocol, such as UUID, password, cipher, auth, or keys.
• Supported transports are TCP, KCP, WebSocket, HTTP Upgrade, XHTTP, HTTP/2, and gRPC. Host, path, header, seed, and mode fields appear only when applicable.
• Stream security supports None, TLS, and Reality where compatible. SNI, ALPN, fingerprint, Reality public key, short ID, and SpiderX must match the provider configuration.
• Hysteria2 supports optional auth, obfuscation, certificate pin, UDP hop ports/interval, and upload/download units k, m, g, or t.
• WireGuard requires Secret Key and Peer Public Key. Pre-Shared Key is optional; Local Addresses may be comma-separated.
• Mux is optional and should be enabled only when supported by the server.

DNSTT
Use ns1;ns2@username:password. Authentication may be entered with the endpoint, and Public Key is required. Configure the resolver separately in the matching DNSTT tweak.

Hysteria1
• Auth only: hy.example.com:443@my-auth.
• Auth + OBFS: hy.example.com:443@my-auth:my-obfs.
• Multiple endpoints may share one port and credentials: hy1.example.com;hy2.example.com:443@my-auth:my-obfs.
Bandwidth uses Upload:Download in Mbps, for example 100:100; one number applies to both directions. ALPN defaults to blank, Allow Insecure defaults to enabled, and Port Hopping Interval defaults to 10 seconds. Configure SNI in the matching Hysteria1 tweak. Hysteria2 belongs under V2Ray.

Category and note
Category is optional. Use the same category on the server and tweak so they are offered together. Note is optional descriptive text.

A tweak defines how a compatible server is reached. Enter a required name, choose the tunnel family and subtype that match the server, then complete only the fields shown for that choice.

IPv4, IPv6, and multiple values
• Separate alternative SNI, Proxy, Bug Host, or resolver values with semicolons or new lines; the app selects a candidate when connecting.
• Host names and IPv4 addresses need no brackets. A host-only IPv6 value is bare, such as 2001:db8::10. Bracket IPv6 whenever a port follows it, such as [2001:db8::10]:8080.
• Multiple IPv6 proxy candidates are valid, for example [2001:db8::10];[2001:db8::11]:8080.
• Placeholder output is IPv6-safe: [host] or [ip] becomes 2001:db8::20, while [host_port], [ssh], or [ip_port] becomes [2001:db8::20]:443.
• Do not add a URL scheme to host-only fields unless a field explicitly shows a URL example.

OpenVPN / SSH
• Template: Use the pills as working starting points for Direct, WebSocket, HTTP Proxy, or TLS/SSL flows.
• Payload: An optional custom HTTP request. Tap the field icon to open the payload generator and its preloaded examples.
• SNI: Normally enter a TLS DNS name. Separate alternatives with semicolons or new lines. This field supports host placeholders, [proxy], [rotate=a;b;c], and [random=a;b;c].
• TLS version: Keep Default unless the endpoint requires a specific supported TLS version.
• Proxy: Use proxy1;proxy2:port@username:password. Credentials are optional. This field supports host placeholders and [sni]; for example, [host]:8080 or [sni]:443.

Dynamic placeholders and where they work
• Payload, SNI, and Proxy: [host] or [ip] inserts the target host. OpenVPN/SSH aliases include [ssh_host] and [bughost].
• SNI: [proxy] inserts the selected proxy host. Rotation and random tags are also supported.
• Proxy: [sni] inserts the selected SNI value.
• Payload only: [port] inserts the target port; [host_port], [ssh], and [ip_port] insert the target host and port.
• Payload only: [proxy], [proxy_host], and [proxy_port] insert configured proxy values; [auth] inserts the Proxy-Authorization header when credentials exist.
• Payload only: [method] = CONNECT; [protocol] = HTTP/1.0; [ua] = device user agent; [raw] = a raw CONNECT request.
• [crlf], [cr], [lf], and [lfcr] insert line breaks.
• [split] sends chunks separately; [delay_split] adds a one-second delay between chunks.
• In payloads, [rotate=a;b;c] cycles through values and [random=a;b;c] chooses one randomly.

Examples
• SNI: [host] or [rotate=sni1.example;sni2.example]
• Proxy: [host]:8080, [sni]:443, or [2001:db8::10]:8080
• Payload: CONNECT [host_port] [protocol][crlf]Host: [bughost][crlf]User-Agent: [ua][crlf][crlf]

V2Ray
Choose Default, VLESS, VMess, Shadowsocks, Socks, HTTP, Trojan, Hysteria2, or WireGuard. Bug Host accepts semicolon-separated candidates such as bug1.example;bug2.example. Put [bughost] in the server V2Ray config where the selected value must be inserted.

DNSTT
Resolver is required and accepts semicolon-separated candidates. Supported examples are DoH https://resolver.example/dns-query, DoT resolver.example:853, and UDP 1.1.1.1:53. Payload is optional and also has the payload generator.

Hysteria1
SNI is optional and belongs in the tweak, so it follows the config's Unlock Payload permission. The TunnelUtils host forms [host], [ip], [ssh_host], [rlb], [bughost], and [cf], their uppercase forms, and the existing extended host aliases all resolve to the selected Hysteria endpoint host inside the native core. [proxy] is not supported for Hysteria. The endpoint, authentication, bandwidth, ALPN, Allow Insecure, and port-hopping interval belong in the matching Hysteria1 server.

Category and note
Category is optional. Use the same category on the tweak and server so they are offered together, for example WS, CF, GCP, Free, or Paid. Note is optional descriptive text.
